boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Saint Mary's Church (Samaria Church) record (June 24, 1864) in Grant's Overland Campaign [May-June 1864]. The June 23 picket fight at the Chickahominy crossing precedes it; Trevilian Station (VA099) is earlier in the same raid. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Divisions and the live field zero. Sheridan says Gregg was attacked by the entire cavalry corps of the enemy while Torbert escorted the trains. Hampton names Gary's and Chambliss's brigades and Wickham's, under Fitzhugh Lee, in the attack, with Lomax left holding the river road.
claims.rationale: Sheridan's 'entire cavalry corps' and Hampton's detachment of Lomax conflict; no counts. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

open_questions: Gregg's, Fitzhugh Lee's, Chambliss's and Gary's reports, the revised return for Sheridan's second expedition (p.186) and Humphreys' Chapter VIII remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan, and it shares headquarters papers with Meade's and Sheridan's reports. Meade's, Sheridan's, Hampton's, Butler's and Wild's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Parts 1 and 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
